correctness.rationale: For a closed rectifiable arclength S² two-design, the H¹ constant-speed F=√3 γ has zero mean, covariance I₃ and |F|²≡3. Orthogonal Fourier projection F=F₁+F₂+R with a+b+c=3 and first/second band covariance ranks ≤2 yields ε=3(L/2π)²−6≥3(2−a)+5c. The fourth-harmonic amplitude of |F₂|² is λ₁(K)−λ₂(K)≥b−2(2−a)≥1−ε/3 by the two-plane trace/eigenvalue principle for U+K+H=I; |F|²≡3 forces that harmonic to be canceled by 2(F₁+F₂)·R+|R|², so amplitude ≤4√(3c)+2c≤4√(3ε/5)+2ε/5. Hence 1≤11ε/15+4√(3ε/5), giving ε≥(1245−180√47)/121 and L≥2π√((1971−180√47)/363)=8.9527209263…; the strict excess over 2π√2 is a genuine uniform positive gap. Eigenvalue inequality and Fourier constants were checked against actual RESULT.md and verify.py. This argument treats every admissible H¹ arclength parameterization, not a finite family or smooth-only subclass.
residual_risks: No claim that numerical lower bound is sharp or the minimizing design exists; spectral hypotheses require exact arclength 2-design and S².
